title: Is Time on China’s Side? Beijing’s Taiwan Calculus and the Balance of Power
summary: Three China specialists argue that Beijing thinks time is on its side over Taiwan, so near-term invasion risk is low, but that the risk rises after 2028 if its non-military pressure fails.

assertions.quote: I will be upfront and say I never believed that war is coming in 2027

verdicts.note: Metaculus's 976 forecasters give a full-scale Chinese invasion of Taiwan 5.3% before 2028 (15% before 2030, 25% before 2035).
On 2026-10-25 Polymarket priced a Chinese offensive to take any part of Taiwan by June 30, 2027 at 5.5% ($520k traded).
FRI's 2024 median expert gave a Chinese invasion of Taiwan 25% before 2030 (superforecasters 19%), well under even odds even over a horizon longer than 2027.

DoD 2025 treats 2027 as a capability goal: China's leaders are 'unsure of the PLA's readiness' and Beijing is refining options to use 'should' leaders decide force is needed, which is no assessment of a decision to invade by 2027.

CSIS takes no position on likelihood but quotes the DoD policy chief (2022): 'I don't think in the next couple of years that they're likely to invade Taiwan'; what is widely accepted is China's determination to develop military options, not a decision to invade.

This is the origin of the 2027 date: Adm. Davidson testified in March 2021 that China 'could attempt' to take Taiwan and the threat is manifest 'in the next six years', a warning of a possible attempt, not a forecast that an invasion will happen.
DDIS says the 2027 target advances modernisation and 'does not mean that China has decided to launch an invasion', peaceful reunification remains preferred, and pursued patiently.
The US intelligence community assesses that Chinese leaders do not currently plan to invade Taiwan in 2027 and have no fixed timeline for unification.

assertions.quote: in the near term there is little risk of a military invasion of Taiwan

verdicts.note: Forecasters and most analysts put an invasion within the next two years at low odds.
Metaculus forecasters put a full-scale invasion of Taiwan at 5.3% before 2028, rising to 15% before 2030 and 25% before 2035: low in the near term.
Polymarket priced a Chinese invasion of Taiwan by mid-2027 at 5.5%, a China-Taiwan military clash before 2027 at 3.8% and a blockade in 2026 at 2.55%.

CSIS records a split: some officials warned of an imminent threat while others (Milley, Kahl, Johnson, Heath) saw no near-term intent; the report itself calls war 'not certain' but 'not unimaginable'.
DDIS judges China currently lacks a successful invasion capability but says the risk of war over Taiwan is steadily increasing and an invasion could come with little warning.
US intelligence expects Beijing to pursue unification short of conflict in 2026 and assesses no current plan to invade in 2027.

assertions.quote: We're talking about a Chinese military that has literally been built to successfully invade Taiwan
Effectively, I think the Chinese are trying to win without fighting.

verdicts.note: Beijing's grey-zone pressure, influence operations and diplomatic isolation of Taiwan are well documented.
DoD says Beijing is trying to compel unification through a concerted pressure campaign combined with positive inducements, not just deter independence, though it is also preparing military options.

DDIS: China applies pressure below the threshold of war to force reunification, with near-daily military activity, influence and diplomatic isolation, and peaceful reunification remains its preferred outcome.
US intelligence says Beijing will keep setting conditions for unification short of conflict and prefers to unify without force if possible.

assertions.quote: I then worry that the risk of conflict or crisis shoots up considerably thereafter

verdicts.note: A conditional forecast that depends on elections and decisions that have not happened yet.

Metaculus invasion probabilities climb from 5.3% before 2028 to 15% before 2030 and 25% before 2035, so the forecast hazard rises after 2028; the condition about Beijing's peaceful pressure failing is not tested.

A former DIA analyst quoted by CSIS argues China will not attack while peaceful unification seems viable but will once it judges force the only option; this matches the conditional mechanism but gives no 2028 date.

assertions.quote: the rate of growth of the PLA's budget has been higher than the rate of growth projected for the economy

verdicts.note: China's announced defence budget has risen about 7 percent a year, above its GDP growth targets of about 5 percent.

China's estimated spending has risen 31 years running (62 percent over 2016-25) but held at 1.7 percent of GDP in 2025, the same as its 2016-24 average, so it has grown roughly in line with the economy, not faster.

assertions.quote: there's no question that the conflict Iran has wasted those assets even further

verdicts.note: Pentagon and think-tank reviews show interceptor and long-range munition stocks drawn down faster than they are replaced.

assertions.quote: a serious Chinese threat to Taiwan is a threat to Japan because of their close proximity

verdicts.note: Prime Minister Takaichi told the Diet in November 2025 that a Taiwan contingency could be a survival-threatening situation for Japan.
US intelligence notes Prime Minister Takaichi in November 2025 called a Chinese invasion of Taiwan a 'survival threatening situation' for Japan, a legal trigger for military action.

assertions.quote: what do they sell the Russians? Stuff that is absolutely legal. Dual use.

verdicts.note: US and EU sanctions findings document Chinese machine tools, electronics and propellant chemicals reaching both countries' arms industries.

DoD 2025: China's state-owned defense firms supplied crucial dual-use components (semiconductors, radars, sensors) for Russia's weapons production; the report also cites sales of dual-use parts for Iran's missile and drone programs.
DDIS: most sanctioned goods Russia uses in the war come from China and Chinese support is crucial to sustaining it; the report says nothing here about Iran.
US intelligence says China's economic support and trade help Russia and Iran withstand sanctions, without specifying dual-use inputs to weapons production.
The US readout expresses deep concern over China's continued support for Russia's defence industrial base; it bears on Russia only (not Iran) and is the US government's position.

assertions.quote: US arms sales to Taiwan should be on the negotiating table between Washington and the PRC

verdicts.note: Based on reported summit readouts and leaks; the substance of the private talks is not public.
